text:
emily: Heads-up — AcmeCorp reported intermittent 401s for signed requests after our last JWKS rotation. They see "invalid_signature" errors. ~3% of requests failed for ~10m across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Escalating.

jason: Do we have logs / example request IDs? Is the token kid missing or mismatched? Any pattern by client SDK version?

emily: Paste from their error bundle (redacted):
```
ERROR verify_jwt: invalid_signature token_kid=rwk_2026_03_09 expected_kid=rwk_2026_03_10
request_id=acme-req-9a1b
client_time_offset=+2s
jwks_fetch_status=200 (cached)
```
They call our hosted API via their proxy; retries often succeed.

rachel: Oncall checked infra logs — our JWKS cache TTL = 300s, but secret rotation happened ~60s after the new keys went live. During that window JWKS fetches from the auth provider returned 504 intermittently. So some nodes kept the old key in cache and continued validating against it.

alex: Also noticed the JWKS fetcher had a backoff flag set after repeated fetch failures; it suppressed fetch attempts for ~5m on some replicas. That left them stuck with stale key despite rotation.

maya: Customer reports: first attempt -> 401 invalid_signature, immediate retry -> 200. So client retry masks this but causes user-facing errors. CS pushed them to increase client retries as a workaround.

jason: Likely contributing factors:
- Key rotation timing + short overlap between old and new keys
- JWKS cache TTL too long for aggressive rotation
- Fetcher backoff logic too punitive on transient upstream errors
- We don't eagerly refetch JWKS when receiving invalid_signature

rachel: Repro steps I used on staging:
1) Start service with jwks cached (old key)
2) Rotate provider keys (new kid)
3) Simulate JWKS provider transient 504 for 60s
4) Send signed request with new kid -> verify fails on nodes with stale cache

I can share the minimal curl that reproduces locally:
```
# token signed with kid=rwk_new
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_WITH_NEW_KID" \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
# expect 401 invalid_signature on stale node
```

alex: Immediate mitigations we can deploy quickly:
- On 401 invalid_signature, trigger an immediate JWKS fetch/refresh (one-shot) and retry the verification before returning upstream 401
- Reduce effective JWKS cache TTL to 60s and honor Cache-Control/ETag from provider
- Relax backoff policy so first failures don't suppress fetches for >30s
- Emit metric jwks_fetch_failures and count of 401_invalid_signature_trigger_refreshed

jason: Long-term: add a rotation webhook from auth provider so we clear caches proactively on rotation. Also add a graceful key overlap policy: accept either old or new kid for X seconds guaranteed.

emily: CS notified AcmeCorp; provided workaround (client exponential retry) and ETA: will push quick patch to canary in ~30m. They accepted that for now but asked for root cause.

deploy-bot: canary deployment queued: eng-runtime/patch-jwks-refresh -> 1/3 hosts (eu-west-1) in 12m

alex: I'll open PR with the immediate patch: 1) trigger refresh on 401 invalid_signature 2) TTL override in config 3) better fetch logging.

rachel: I'll monitor canary and set an alert for jwks_fetch_failures > 0.5% and 401 invalid_signature spike.

maya: Please paste the request_id from the earlier error once you have logs so I can forward to the customer for traceability.

emily: request_id=acme-req-9a1b (from earlier). Thanks everyone — will post an incident summary after canary verification.

jason: Also add an internal runbook note: when rotating keys, schedule a rolling cache invalidation and pause aggressive backoff on JWKS fetcher for 5m.

rachel: Will follow-up with a short postmortem. For now, mitigation plan: canary -> global deploy if green -> rotation webhook work in next sprint.
